text: Every penny in your change cost America almost 4 cents to make, so why keep making it?
In 2024, the mints spent about 3.7 cents on each one-cent coin, a loss on every single one.
Losing money to make money. Bold. So why didn't they stop sooner?
Pennies go back to 1793. Habit, tradition, and partly a fear that shops would round prices
up. Then the treasury placed its final order for penny blanks. The last one was struck
in Philadelphia in November 2025. And here's the coin that's even worse. The nickel
also costs more than 5 cents to make. And it's still being made. That's the mirage.
A coin's value is printed on it, not built into it.
Over 114 billion pennies are still out there, still legal tender.
Finally, a coin with a worse job than me!
Comment, do you still use pennies?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
